questions: When the game ends because S becomes empty, does the player who performed the last operation win immediately, or is there a check after the operation that S is empty? (i.e., does the operation that makes S empty count as a winning move?)
Is the set S initially empty, and does the condition 'If S=' refer to S being empty at any point, or specifically after the operation? The clarification doesn't address this.
Does 'S=' mean S is the empty set? The notation is ambiguous; it might be a typo for 'S = {}' or 'S is empty'.
Can a player choose an index i that is already in S? The operation says 'if i∉ S, add i to S', but it doesn't forbid choosing i ∈ S.
Is the game guaranteed to end? The prompt says 'it can be proven that until a winner is determined... players can always make a move', but doesn't explicitly state the game always ends.
What happens if after subtracting 1 from A_i, A_i becomes 0? Can that index still be chosen in future turns? The operation requires A_i ≥ 1 to choose i.
Does the order of players matter if the game ends on the first move? For example, if initial S is empty and a move makes S non-empty, does the game continue?
Is the set S modified only when i∉ S, or is there any other way S changes? The operation description is clear, but could there be implicit removals?
